rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At death the soul reaches the clavicles, the upper part of the chest.
rows.anchor: يعني بلوغ الروح عند موته إلى التراقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tarquwa is the singular form of the plural taraqi, clavicles.
rows.anchor: وهي أعلى الصدر ، واحدها ترقوه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The dying person’s family asks who can perform incantations for him using God’s beautiful names.
rows.anchor: من راق يرقيه بالرقى وأسماء الله الحسنى ، قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو قلابة
rows.claim: Raqin here means a physician who can heal.
rows.anchor: من طبيب شاف ، قاله أبو قلابة

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited poet asks whether any healer can avert death, using raqi for a healer.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر : هل للفتى من بنات الدهر من واقى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Abu al-Jawza reports Ibn Abbas’s view that angels ask which angel will ascend with the soul, angels of mercy or punishment.
rows.anchor: ملائكة الرحمة أو ملائكة العذاب , رواه أبو الجوزاء عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He becomes certain that he is leaving this world.
rows.anchor: أي تيقن أنه مفارق الدنيا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The legs joining together signifies this world joining the next.
rows.anchor: اتصال الدنيا بالآخرة , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد
rows.claim: It can mean hardship compounded: the agony of death joined to the terror of the next life.
rows.anchor: وهو شدة كرب الموت بشدة هول المطلع , قاله عكرمة ومجاهد

rows.speaker: حذيفة بن أنس الهذلي
rows.claim: The Hudhayli poet compares war’s urgency to war baring its leg, illustrating the image of hardship.
rows.anchor: قول حذيفة بن أنس الهذلي : أخو الحرب إن عضت به الحرب عضها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the phrase literally: the dying person’s legs twist together.
rows.anchor: الثالث : التفت ساقاه عند الموت

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba cites some exegetes who say the leg twisting occurred at the primordial covenant.
rows.anchor: وحكى ابن قتيبة عن بعض المفسرين أن التفاف الساق بالساق عند الميثاق

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says the man’s legs died and could no longer carry him, though he had walked on them extensively.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : ماتت رجلاه فلم تحملاه

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Two severe events converge: people prepare the body while angels prepare the soul.
rows.anchor: الناس يجهزون جسده , والملائكة يجهزون روحه , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: خارجة
rows.claim: Al-masaq means the departure or onward journey.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : المنطلق , قاله خارجة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Al-masaq means the final resting place.
rows.anchor: الثاني : المستقر , قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage is about Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: هذا في أبي جهل , وفيه وجهان

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He neither believed God’s Book nor prayed to God.
rows.anchor: فلا صدق بكتاب الله ولا صلى لله , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He neither believed the message nor believed the One who sent the messenger.
rows.anchor: فلا صدق بالرسالة ولا آمن بالمرسل , وهو معنى قول الكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible synthesis is that he did not believe in his heart or act with his body.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : فلا آمن بقلبه ولا عمل ببدنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is that he called the Messenger a liar and turned away from the One who sent him.
rows.anchor: كذب الرسول وتولى عن المرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is that he rejected the Quran and turned away from obedience.
rows.anchor: كذب بالقرآن وتولى عن الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person strutting off to his family is Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: يعني أبا جهل ، وفيه ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Yatamatta means that he was conceited in himself.
rows.anchor: يختال في نفسه ، قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: It means walking with a swagger, described as the gait of Banu Makhzum.
rows.anchor: يتبختر في مشيته ، قال زيد بن أسلم وهي مشية بني مخزوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation derives it from bending one’s back, since al-mata means the back.
rows.anchor: أن يلوي مطاه ، والمطا : الظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text notes a prohibition on the gait called al-matitaa, in which a man swings his hands while walking.
rows.anchor: وجاء النهي عن مشية المطيطاء وذلك أن الرجل يلقي يديه مع الكفين في مشيه

rows.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: They report that the Prophet met swaggering Abu Jahl at Mecca’s Batha, pushed his chest and poked him while saying the warning; Abu Jahl taunted him, and the verses were revealed.
rows.anchor: حكى الكلبي ومقاتل : أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لقي أبا جهل ببطحاء مكة وهو يتبختر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: One gloss is that evil is near to him; Qatada calls it one threat following another.
rows.anchor: وليك الشر , قال قتادة , وهذا وعيد على وعيد

rows.speaker: الخنساء
rows.claim: A second gloss takes awla as woe to you, supported by al-Khansa’s poetic usage.
rows.anchor: الثاني : ويل لك , قالت الخنساء :

rows.speaker: الخنساء
rows.claim: Al-Khansa’s line uses awla in the sense of woe to oneself, supporting the preceding gloss.
rows.anchor: هممت بنفسي بعض الهموم … فأولى لنفسي أولى لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ala can mean a condition or circumstance, and also the bier on which the dead are carried.
rows.anchor: الآلة : الحالة , والآلة : السرير أيضا الذي يحمل عليه الموتى

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: One view asks whether a person thinks no deed will be required of him.
rows.anchor: فهل لا يفترض عليه عمل , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Another view is that a person thinks he will not be resurrected.
rows.anchor: يظن ألا يبعث , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: A third view takes sada as being left without commands or prohibitions.
rows.anchor: ملغى لا يؤمر ولا ينهى , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth view is that a person is left without reckoning or punishment; the cited poet says God leaves nothing neglected.
rows.anchor: عبث لا يحاسب ولا يعاقب , قال الشاعر : فأقسم بالله جهد اليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of yumna is that semen is poured out; Mina is said to take its name from the spilling of blood there.
rows.anchor: أن معنى يمنى يراق , ولذلك سميت منى لإراقة الدماء فيها

rows.speaker: يزيد بن عامر
rows.claim: A second explanation is that yumna means to be brought forth or created; Yazid’s verse uses it for what the maker brings about.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول يزيد بن عامر : فاسلك طريقك تمشي غير مختشع حتى تلاقي ما يمني لك الماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation is that it means to combine, referring to the mingling of male and female fluid.
rows.anchor: بمعنى يشترك أي اشتراك ماء الرجل بماء المرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After being a drop of semen, the human becomes a clinging clot.
rows.anchor: يعني أنه كان بعد النطفة علقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possibility is that God creates him in the womb before birth, then proportions him after birth as strength and movement mature.
rows.anchor: خلق من الأرحام قبل الولادة وسوي بعدها عند استكمال القوة وتمام الحركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that God creates bodies and fits them for action, assigning each limb its function.
rows.anchor: خلق الأجسام وسواها للأفعال , فجعل لكل جارحة عملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier generations are sinners; they may mean Noah’s people, whose Flood destruction was especially famous and comprehensive.
rows.anchor: يعني من العصاة ، وفيمن أريد بهم وجهان : أحدهما : قوم نوح عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they are the peoples of every prophet who were annihilated, a more particular application to those communities.
rows.anchor: أنه قوم كل نبي استؤصلوا , لأنه في خصوص الأمم أندر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Later sinners are made to follow the earlier ones in destruction for their sins, by sword or other ruin.
rows.anchor: يعني في هلاكهم بالمعصية كالأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possibility is a threat of worldly destruction meant to serve as a warning.
rows.anchor: تهويل لهلاكهم في الدنيا اعتبارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse reports the punishment they deserve in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: إخبار بعذابهم في الآخرة استحقاقا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Mihin water is the pure or selected part of the fluid.
rows.anchor: من صفوة الماء , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mihin means weak or lowly water.
rows.anchor: من ماء ضعيف , قاله مجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: ابن كامل
rows.claim: Mihin means flowing semen.
rows.anchor: من مني سائل , قاله ابن كامل

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: The secure resting place is the mother’s womb, where the fetus is protected from heat and cold.
rows.anchor: قاله وهب بن منبه في رحم أمه لا يؤذيه حر ولا برد

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Makin means secure: the fluid does not flow back out or spread through the body, so it remains there.
rows.anchor: مكين حريز لا يعود فيخرج ولا يبث في الجسد فيدوم , قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The known appointed term is the day of birth.
rows.anchor: إلى يوم ولادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi reads qaddarna with a doubled d; the other readers read qadarna lightly.
rows.anchor: في قراءة نافع مشددة , وقرأ الباقون مخففة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the light reading, the phrase means We mastered or owned, and excellent are the Masters.
rows.anchor: فمن قرأ بالتخفيف فتأويلها : فملكنا فنعم المالكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the doubled reading, it means We decreed, and excellent are the Deciders.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ بالتشديد فتأويلها : فقضينا فنعم القاضون

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says the two forms are dialect variants with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : هما لغتان ومعناهما واحد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas offers the gloss كنا for kifatan.
rows.anchor: يعني كنا , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Kifatan can mean a covering.
rows.anchor: غطاء , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: المفضل
rows.claim: Kifatan can mean a gathering place.
rows.anchor: قاله المفضل . الرابع : وعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth gloss is a receptacle or container, cited with the poet al-Simsama ibn al-Tirimmih.
rows.anchor: الرابع : وعاء قال الصمصامة بن الطرماح

rows.speaker: مبشر بن عبيد
rows.claim: Mubashir ibn Ubayd locates the holy valley at Aylah.
rows.anchor: وهو قول مبشر بن عبيد هو واد بأيلة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan locates the holy valley in Palestine.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الحسن , هو واد بفلسطين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Muqaddas means blessed.
rows.anchor: المبارك , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Muqaddas means purified; Hasan says it was sanctified twice.
rows.anchor: المطهر , قاله الحسن : قدس مرتين

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة وعكرمة
rows.claim: One view takes Tuwa as the proper name of the holy valley.
rows.anchor: أنه أسم الوادي المقدس , قاله مجاهد وقتادة وعكرمة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another view derives it from Moses passing through or traversing the valley.
rows.anchor: لأنه مر بالوادي فطواه , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says the valley was folded or enveloped in blessing.
rows.anchor: لأنه طوي بالبركة , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد
rows.claim: Another interpretation commands Moses to tread the valley with his foot.
rows.anchor: يعني طأ الوادي بقدمك , قاله عكرمة ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that its sanctification was multiplied until it was purified of sins, by analogy with folding a book.
rows.anchor: من دنس المعاصي , مأخوذ من طي الكتاب إذا ضوعف

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Tazakka here means to become Muslim.
rows.anchor: إلى أن تسلم , قال قتادة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Tazakka can mean to do good.
rows.anchor: إلى أن تعمل خيرا ، قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: The great sign is Moses’ staff and hand.
rows.anchor: أنها عصاه ويده ، قاله الحسن وقتادة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: The great sign refers to Paradise and Hell.
rows.anchor: أنها الجنة والنار ، قاله السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third possibility is God’s speech to Moses from the tree.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : أنه كلامه من الشجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that Pharaoh assembled the sorcerers for a contest and summoned his army to fight.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : حشر السحرة للمعارضة ، ونادى جنده للمحاربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he gathered the people to attend and addressed them.
rows.anchor: حشر الناس للحضور ونادى أي خطب فيهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The punishment covers this world and the next: drowning in this life and fire in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: عقوبة الدنيا والآخرة , قال قتادة : عذبه الله في الدنيا بالغرق وفي الآخرة بالنار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The phrase can mean punishment at the beginning and end of Pharaoh’s life.
rows.anchor: عذاب أول عمره وآخره , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima identifies the earlier claim as I am unaware of any god for you but me, and the later one as I am your highest lord.
rows.anchor: الأولى قوله : ( ما علمت لكم من إله غيري ) والآخرة قوله ( أنا ربكم الأعلى ) , قاله عكرمة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the two claims were forty years apart, while Mujahid and al-Suddi give thirty years.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : وكان بينهما أربعون سنة , وقال مجاهد : ثلاثون سنة , قال السدي : وهي الآخرة

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: The first punishment was respite, and the last was Hell, as described in 40:46.
rows.anchor: النار يعرضون عليها } الآية , قاله الربيع

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada’s account identifies Ibn Umm Maktum as blind Abdallah ibn Zaida of Banu Fihr, who came to ask the Prophet to teach recitation while he spoke with Quraysh leaders hoping they would convert.
rows.anchor: روى سعيد عن قتادة أن ابن أم مكتوم , وهو عبد الله بن زائدة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies the Quraysh leader speaking with the Prophet as Umayya ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : هو أمية بن خلف

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the two Quraysh leaders were Utba and Shayba, sons of Rabi'a.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : هما عتبة وشيبة ابنا ربيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet frowned and turned away from the blind man, and God reproached him for doing so.
rows.anchor: فأعرض النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الأعمى وعبس في وجهه , فعاتبه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blind man is Ibn Umm Maktum.
rows.anchor: يعني ابن أم مكتوم

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Yazakka can mean to believe.
rows.anchor: يؤمن , قاله عطاء

rows.speaker: ابن عيسى
rows.claim: It can mean to worship through good deeds.
rows.anchor: يتعبد بالأعمال الصالحة ، قاله ابن عيسى

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: It can mean to memorize the Quran being recited to him.
rows.anchor: يحفظ ما يتلوه عليه من القرآن ، قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن شجرة
rows.claim: It can mean to gain understanding of religion.
rows.anchor: يتفقه في الدين , قاله ابن شجرة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi reads the sense as perhaps he is purified and remembers, and says the alif is connective or extra.
rows.anchor: قال السدي : لعله يزكى ويذكر , والألف صلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dhikra can mean understanding of religion or admonition.
rows.anchor: وفي الذكرى وجهان : أحدها : الفقه . الثاني : العظة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet would spread his cloak for Ibn Umm Maktum to sit on when he saw him approach, honoring him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : فكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا نظر إليه مقبلا بسط له رداءه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the Prophet appointed Ibn Umm Maktum to lead the people’s prayers in Medina during two military expeditions.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : واستخلفه على صلاة الناس بالمدينة في غزاتين من غزواته

rows.speaker: الفراء والكلبي
rows.claim: One view takes the reminder to be this surah.
rows.anchor: أن هذه السورة تذكرة , قاله الفراء والكلبي

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Another view takes the reminder to be the Quran.
rows.anchor: أن القرآن تذكرة , قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: One gloss is that God inspires remembrance in whoever He wills.
rows.anchor: فمن شاء الله ألهمه الذكر , قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Alternatively, God reminds whoever wishes to remember through the Quran.
rows.anchor: فمن شاء أن يتذكر بالقرآن أذكره الله , وهو معنى قول الكلبي

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: The scrolls are honored by God.
rows.anchor: مكرمة عند الله , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: The scrolls are honored in religion because they contain wisdom and knowledge.
rows.anchor: مكرمة في الدين لما فيها من الحكم والعلم , قاله الطبري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that the honored scrolls are those carried down by noble keepers; a book’s honor comes from its author.
rows.anchor: لأنه نزل بها كرام الحفظة . ويحتمل قولا رابعا : أنها نزلت من كريم

rows.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
rows.claim: The scrolls are raised in heaven.
rows.anchor: مرفوعة في السماء , قاله يحيى بن سلام

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: The scrolls are elevated in status and renown.
rows.anchor: مرفوعة القدر والذكر , قاله الطبري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that they are above ambiguity and contradiction.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل قولا ثالثا : مرفوعة عن الشبه والتناقض

rows.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
rows.claim: They are clean of physical impurity.
rows.anchor: من الدنس , قاله يحيى بن سلام

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: They are purified from idolatry.
rows.anchor: من الشرك , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: They are such that only the purified touch them.
rows.anchor: أنه لا يمسها إلا المطهرون , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: They are purified by being kept from descent upon polytheists.
rows.anchor: مطهرة من أن تنزل على المشركين , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that a pure sender sent it down with a pure angel to a pure messenger.
rows.anchor: لأنها نزلت من طاهر مع طاهر على طاهر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Safara means scribes; al-Mufaddal derives it from safara, to write.
rows.anchor: أن السفرة الكتبة , قاله ابن عباس , قال المفضل : هو مأخوذ من سفر يسفر سفرا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj links the term to making something clear, as the dawn brightens, and to a woman unveiling her face.
rows.anchor: من تبيين الشيء وإيضاحه , كما يقال أسفر الصبح إذا وضح ضياؤه وظهر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Safara can mean reciters because they read the scriptures.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أنهم القراء , قال قتادة لأنهم يقرؤون الأسفار

rows.speaker: زيد
rows.claim: Another view identifies the safara as angels who mediate between God and His messengers with mercy.
rows.anchor: الثالث : هم الملائكة , لأنهم السفرة بين يدي الله ورسله بالرحمة , قال زيد

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra cites a poet’s use of sifara for mediation between a people.
rows.anchor: سفر بين القوم إذا بلغ صلاحا , وأنشد الفراء

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Kiram means honored by their Lord.
rows.anchor: كرام على ربهم , قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: They are noble by abstaining from sins and raising themselves above them.
rows.anchor: كرام عن المعاصي فهم يرفعون أنفسهم عنها , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak’s explanation is that they show considerate concealment and protection toward someone who has been intimate with his wife.
rows.anchor: يتكرمون على من باشر زوجته بالستر عليه دفاعا عنه وصيانة له , وهو معنى قول الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that they prefer others’ benefits to their own.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل رابعا : أنهم يؤثرون منافع غيرهم على منافع أنفسهم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Barara means obedient.
rows.anchor: أحدها : مطيعين , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Barara means truthful and maintaining ties or goodness.
rows.anchor: الثاني : صادقين واصلين , قاله الطبري

rows.speaker: ابن شجرة
rows.claim: Barara means pious and purified.
rows.anchor: الثالث : متقين مطهرين , قاله ابن شجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-abrar are those whose goodness extends to others, while al-khayyira are good only to themselves.
rows.anchor: أن البررة من تعدى خيرهم إلى غيرهم , والخيرة من كان خيرهم مقصورا عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutila can mean punished or cursed.
rows.anchor: في ( قتل ) وجهان : أحدهما : عذب . الثاني : لعن

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Al-Insan can refer to every disbeliever.
rows.anchor: أنه إشارة إلى كل كافر , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the person as Umayya ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: أنه أمية بن خلف , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن جريج والكلبي
rows.claim: They identify him as Utba ibn Abi Lahab, who declared disbelief in the Lord of the setting star; the Prophet prayed against him and a lion killed him on the road to Syria.
rows.anchor: فأخذه الأسد في طريق الشام , قاله ابن جريج والكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On an exclamatory reading, the Arabs’ curse-like expressions show wonder: marvel at how ungrateful the human is after the blessings listed next.
rows.anchor: أن ( ما ) تعجب , وعادة العرب إذا تعجبوا من شيء قالوا قاتله الله ما أحسنه

rows.speaker: السدي ويحيى بن سلام
rows.claim: They read ma as an interrogative: what thing made him disbelieve?
rows.anchor: أي شيء أكفره , على وجه الاستفهام , قاله السدي ويحيى بن سلام

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: A third interpretation is how accursed he is.
rows.anchor: ما ألعنه , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك
rows.claim: The path made easy is the route of birth from the mother’s womb.
rows.anchor: خروجه من بطن أمه , قاله عكرمة والضحاك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The path can mean the path of happiness or misery.
rows.anchor: سبيل السعادة والشقاوة , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The path can mean the path of guidance or misguidance.
rows.anchor: سبيل الهدى والضلالة , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that God makes easy the paths of a person’s benefits and harms.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل رابعا : سبيل منافعه ومضاره

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: God made the human a person with a grave in which to be buried.
rows.anchor: جعله ذا قبر يدفن فيه , قاله الطبري

rows.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
rows.claim: Alternatively, God made people who bury and conceal the dead.
rows.anchor: جعل من يقبره ويواريه , قاله يحيى بن سلام

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-A'sha’s verse says that a dead person placed against her chest would live and never be carried to a grave, illustrating burial.
rows.anchor: قال الأعشى : لو أسندت ميتا إلى نحرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ansharahu means that God brought the dead person back to life.
rows.anchor: يعني أحياه , قال الأعشى : حتى يقول الناس مما رأوا

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-A'sha’s poem calls a dead person who rises the resurrected dead.
rows.anchor: يا عجبا للميت الناشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poet contrasts being seized through the back with being seized through the breast area, using tarā'ib for a torso location.
rows.anchor: فإن تدبروا نأخذكم في ظهوركم … وإن تقبلوا نأخذكم في الترائب

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Tarā'ib can mean the area from the shoulder blades to the chest.
rows.anchor: ما بين المنكبين إلى الصدر , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Tarā'ib can mean the place where a necklace rests; a poem locates saffron on the breast and neck.
rows.anchor: موضع القلادة , قاله ابن عباس , قال الشاعر : والزعفران على ترائبها

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr identifies the tarā'ib as four lower ribs; al-Zajjaj specifies four ribs on each side of the chest.
rows.anchor: أنها أربعة أضلاع من الجانب الأسفل , قاله ابن جبير , وحكى الزجاج

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Tarā'ib can mean the region between the hands, feet, and eyes.
rows.anchor: بين اليدين والرجلين والعينين , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: معمر بن أبي حبيبة
rows.claim: Tarā'ib can mean the heart’s essence.
rows.anchor: هي عصارة القلب , قاله معمر بن أبي حبيبة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: God is able to return semen to the urethra.
rows.anchor: على أن يرد المني في الإحليل , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: God is able to return the fluid to the backbone.
rows.anchor: على أن يرد الماء في الصلب , قاله عكرمة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: God is able to return a person from old age to youth, childhood, and finally the semen stage.
rows.anchor: من الصبا إلى النطفة , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة وقتادة
rows.claim: God is able to resurrect a person alive after death.
rows.anchor: على أن يعيده حيا بعد موته , قاله الحسن وعكرمة وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that God can hold back the fluid so that it does not emerge.
rows.anchor: على أن يحبس الماء فلا يخرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is return to earthly life after resurrection, which disbelievers will request.
rows.anchor: على أن يعيده إلى الدنيا بعد بعثه في الآخرة لأن الكفار يسألون الله فيها الرجعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hidden matters will be exposed.
rows.anchor: يوم تبلى السرائر } أي تظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the hidden matters are tested by being exposed in the afterlife after concealment in this world.
rows.anchor: أن تبتلى بظهور السرائر في الآخرة بعد استتارها في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view defines secrets as everything a person hides, good or evil, including belief or disbelief; al-Ahwas’s verse supports this sense.
rows.anchor: كل ما استتر به الإنسان من خير وشر , وأضمره من إيمان أو كفر , كما قال الأحوص

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam transmits a Prophetic report that three trusts are prayer, fasting, and major impurity; a person may falsely claim to have prayed, fasted, or performed ghusl.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( الأمانات ثلاث : الصلاة والصوم والجنابة

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Qawwa means one’s clan and nasir means an ally.
rows.anchor: أن القوة العشيرة , والناصر : الحليف , قاله سفيان

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Alternatively, no bodily strength can protect him, and no other person can prevent God’s punishment or prevail against God.
rows.anchor: فما له من قوة في بدنه , ولا ناصر من غيره يمتنع به من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that he has no means of avoiding punishment and no advocate to argue for him.
rows.anchor: فما له من قوة في الامتناع , ولا ناصر في الاحتجاج

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The sky’s returning quality is its rain, which returns every year.
rows.anchor: ذات المطر , لأنه يرجع في كل عام , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view takes the phrase as clouds because they return with rain.
rows.anchor: ذات السحاب , لأنه يرجع بالمطر

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: The sky returns to the state it had before.
rows.anchor: ذات الرجوع إلى ما كانت , قاله عكرمة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: The phrase can refer to the returning stars.
rows.anchor: ذات النجوم الراجعة , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that it means angels who return to heaven with people’s deeds; this is an oath.
rows.anchor: ذات الملائكة لرجوعهم إليها بأعمال العباد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The earth’s fissuring refers to plants emerging as it splits.
rows.anchor: ذات النبات لانصداع الأرض عنه , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: The phrase can refer to valleys, which split the earth.
rows.anchor: ذات الأودية , لأن الأرض قد انصدعت بها , قاله ابن جريج

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The phrase can refer to roads made by travelers splitting the ground.
rows.anchor: ذات الطرق التي تصدعها المشاة , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view refers to cultivated land because plowing opens the soil.
rows.anchor: ذات الحرث لأنه يصدعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is the earth splitting open to release the dead for resurrection; both this and the previous item are oaths.
rows.anchor: ذات الأموات , لانصداعها عنهم للنشور وهذان قسمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view connects the decisive word to the preceding threat of resurrection and disclosure of secrets, confirming that warning.
rows.anchor: ما قدمه عن الوعيد من قوله تعالى : ( إنه على رجعه لقادر يوم تبلى السرائر ) الآية .

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: On the preceding-threat interpretation, fasl means a boundary or decisive limit.
rows.anchor: أحدها : حد , قاله ابن جبير

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: On the preceding-threat interpretation, fasl means just judgment.
rows.anchor: الثاني : عدل , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view takes the decisive word to be the Quran, confirming its revealed Book.
rows.anchor: القول : ان المراد بالفصل القرآن تصديقا لكتابه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: On the Quran interpretation, fasl means truth.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : حق , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ali reports hearing the Prophet say that God’s Book contains the history of those before and judgment for those after, is decisive and no jest, and guides; abandoning it or seeking guidance elsewhere brings ruin.
rows.anchor: ما رواه الحارث عن علي قال : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Al-hazl means play or frivolity.
rows.anchor: باللعب ، قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد

rows.speaker: وكيع والضحاك
rows.claim: Al-hazl can mean falsehood.
rows.anchor: بالباطل ، قاله وكيع والضحاك

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-hazl can mean lying.
rows.anchor: بالكذب ، قاله السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Mecca plotted against the Prophet in the council house at Dar al-Nadwa, as also stated in 8:30.
rows.anchor: يعني أهل مكة حين اجتمعوا في دار الندوة على المكر برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s counterplot means retribution by fire in the afterlife and by the sword in this world.
rows.anchor: يعني بالانتقام في الآخرة بالنار , وفي الدنيا بالسيف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ruwaydan can mean soon or near in time.
rows.anchor: قريبا , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruwaydan can mean waiting; the cited poet tells someone to wait until the haze clears.
rows.anchor: رويدك حتى تنطوي ثم تنجلي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Ruwaydan can mean a little while.
rows.anchor: قليلا , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the disbelievers were killed at Badr.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك : فقتلوا يوم بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view treats mahhil and amhil as two synonymous forms.
rows.anchor: أنهما لغتان معناهما واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another distinguishes them: mahhil means refrain from harming them, while amhil means await their punishment.
rows.anchor: فمهل الكف عنهم , وأمهل انتظار العذاب لهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: A second etymology derives Quran from qara'a meaning to gather and join together, since its verses are collected; Qatada’s poetry compares this with a womb gathering a child.
rows.anchor: وهو قول قتادة ، أنه مصدر من قولك قرأت الشيء ، إذا جمعته وضممت بعضه إلى بعض

rows.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
rows.claim: Amr ibn Kulthum’s verse uses qara'at for a womb that has not gathered a child, supporting the gathering etymology.
rows.anchor: كما قال عمرو بن كلثوم : تريك إذا دخلت على خلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Furqan names the Quran because God separates truth from falsehood; this is the consensus, since the root means separation.
rows.anchor: فلأن الله عز وجل فرق بين الحق والباطل ، وهو قول الجماعة ، لأن أصل الفرقان هو الفرق بين شيئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kitab derives from writing or gathering letters together; it is called a book even when already written.
rows.anchor: فلأنه مصدر من قولك كتبت كتابا ، والكتاب هو خط الكاتب حروف المعجم مجموعة ومتفرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr may mean a reminder from God teaching servants duties and limits, or honor and renown for believers; the latter is linked to 43:44.
rows.anchor: حدوده . والثاني : أنه ذكر وشرف وفخر

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra derives Torah from the expression for a firebrand giving off fire, so the name means illumination.
rows.anchor: فإن الفراء يجعلها مشتقة من قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zabur derives from the verb for writing a book; a poet compares the image of dwellings to a written mark.
rows.anchor: وأما الزبور ، فإنه مشتق من قولهم : زبر الكتاب يزبره إذا كتبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Injil derives from extracting something, as a man’s offspring are called his extracted progeny; a poem illustrates the usage.
rows.anchor: فهو مأخوذ من نجلت الشيء ، إذا أخرجته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is a miracle proving its revelation, protected from alteration, and a proof of the Messenger’s truth; it contains clear and obscure material.
rows.anchor: وخصه بمعجز دل على تنزيله ، ومنع من تبديله ، وبين به صدق رسوله ، وجعل ما استودعه على نوعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People share in understanding the clear material, while scholars interpret the obscure, so the miracle reaches all and degrees of distinction remain.
rows.anchor: يشترك الناس في علم جلية ويختص العلماء بتأويل خفية حتى يعم الإعجاز ، ثم يحصل التفاضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentator limits this work to obscure interpretation, drawing on transmitted reports and reasoning, collecting earlier and later views, and marking his own conjectures as possibilities.
rows.anchor: جعلت كتابي هذا مقصورا على تأويل ما خفي علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He omits what is already apparent from the wording so that the commentary is easier to consult and understand.
rows.anchor: وعدلت عما ظهر معناه من فحواه اكتفاء بفهم قارئه وتصور تالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He precedes the commentary with foundational chapters that clarify difficult interpretations and hidden evidence.
rows.anchor: وقدمت لتفسيره فصولا ، تكون لعمله أصولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran has four names in the Book: Quran, Furqan, Book, and Reminder, supported by citations including this verse.
rows.anchor: سمى الله القرآن في كتابه بأربعة أسماء

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas derives Quran from qara'a meaning to make clear, citing the command to follow its recitation as an instruction to act on what God explains.
rows.anchor: وهو قول عبد الله بن عباس ، مصدر من قولك قرأت أي بينت ، استشهادا بقوله تعالى : ^ ( فإذا قرأناه فاتبع قرآنه
